title: Grünbaum Lower Bound — Constructing Point Sets with ≫ n^{3/2} Four-Point Lines

problemStatement.formal: For a finite P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 with |P| = n and no 5 collinear, let f_4(P) = \#\{S \in \binom{P}{4} : S \text{ collinear}\}. Prove the lower bound: there is c > 0 such that for infinitely many n, some P_n with |P_n| = n and no 5 collinear satisfies f_4(P_n) \ge c\,n^{3/2}; i.e. \max f_4 = \Omega(n^{3/2}) via an explicit Grünbaum-style construction.
problemStatement.plain: The parent proof gives upper bounds on how many lines pass through exactly four points of a no-five-collinear planar set. This problem asks for the complementary lower bound: build explicit point configurations containing on the order of n^{3/2} four-point lines, formalizing Grünbaum's construction.
whyMatters: n^{3/2} is the historical heart of Erdős #101 ($100 prize): Erdős conjectured Θ(n^{3/2}) precisely because Grünbaum's construction matched it from below.
Provides the first proven, machine-checked lower bound to sit against the parent proof's n(n-1)/12 upper bound, sandwiching the extremal function.

Exercises constructive incidence geometry in Lean (explicit coordinates, counting collinear 4-tuples), a capability the gallery currently lacks, and is a stepping stone toward the harder Solymosi–Stojaković construction.
